objective: Build a minimal "Hello World" web page served by Nginx, including the HTML content, Nginx configuration, and a Dockerized deployment setup for easy local running.

managers.name: delivery_lead
managers.title: Delivery Lead
managers.description: Ensures all files are correct, consistent, and the project can be spun up with a single command.

sub_agents.name: web_developer
sub_agents.description: Creates HTML/CSS content and Nginx configuration files. Outputs complete, ready-to-use config and markup files.

sub_agents.name: infra_engineer
sub_agents.description: Creates Docker and deployment artifacts for running the Nginx server locally. Outputs Dockerfiles and helper scripts.

reviewers.name: security_engineer
reviewers.title: Senior Security Engineer
reviewers.description: Review for OWASP Top 10, broken auth, secrets exposure, input validation, least privilege. Think like an attacker.

reviewers.name: ux_designer
reviewers.title: Senior UX/UI Designer
reviewers.description: Review for WCAG 2.1 AA, visual hierarchy, information architecture, cognitive load, interaction quality.

reviewers.name: user_tester
reviewers.title: End-User Representative
reviewers.description: Review as a non-technical first-time user: clarity, plain language, workflow intuitiveness, value delivered.

reviewers.name: creative_director
reviewers.title: Creative Director
reviewers.description: Challenge conventional thinking. Is this the obvious boring solution or something genuinely clever? Push for innovation, elegance, and delight. Ask: what would make someone say 'that's brilliant'? FLAG safe, generic, or copy-paste solutions that lack originality or miss creative opportunities.

reviewers.name: devils_advocate
reviewers.title: Devil's Advocate
reviewers.description: Assume everything is wrong. Find the hidden assumptions, logical flaws, unstated dependencies, and failure modes nobody mentioned. Ask: what happens when this breaks at 3am? What did they forget? What looks right but is subtly wrong? Be ruthless but specific — vague skepticism is useless.

reviewers.name: performance_engineer
reviewers.title: Performance Engineer
reviewers.description: Review for scalability, efficiency, and production readiness. Find N+1 queries, unbounded loops, memory leaks, missing indexes, chatty APIs, blocking calls in async paths, missing caching, and anything that will fall over at 10x traffic. Think in terms of p99 latency and cost per request.

tasks.title: Create Hello World HTML page
tasks.description: Write a clean, minimal `index.html` file that displays "Hello, World!" with basic styling. The page should have a proper HTML5 doctype, a centered heading, and a short subtitle line like "Served by Nginx". Save to `src/index.html`.

tasks.title: Write Nginx configuration
tasks.description: Write an `nginx.conf` file that serves the static `index.html` on port 80. Use a simple single-server block listening on port 80, with root pointing to `/usr/share/nginx/html`. Include a proper `location /` block. Save to `nginx/nginx.conf`.

tasks.title: Create Dockerfile and docker-compose
tasks.description: Create a `Dockerfile` based on `nginx:alpine` that copies `src/index.html` to `/usr/share/nginx/html/` and copies `nginx/nginx.conf` to `/etc/nginx/nginx.conf`. Also create a `docker-compose.yml` that builds the image and maps host port 8080 to container port 80. Save both files to the project root.

tasks.title: Write README with run instructions
tasks.description: Write a `README.md` that explains the project, lists the file structure, and provides step-by-step instructions to run with `docker-compose up --build` and verify by visiting `http://localhost:8080`. Keep it concise.
